title: EFAST (Extended FAST)

blocks.x: Penetrating chest/abdominal injury or hypotensive blunt trauma. Patient is hemodynamically unstable.
RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT (RUQ) (Morison’s Pouch): A distinct dependent band of anechoic free fluid is visualized within the hepatorenal recess measuring up to 1.8 cm in maximal depth.
LEFT UPPER QUADRANT (LUQ): Trace free fluid noted superior to the spleen in the left subphrenic space.
SUPRAPUBIC (PELVIS): Moderately sized fluid collection pooling in the retrovesical/rectouterine space.
Normal right ventricular wall motion; no circumferential or localized pericardial effusion.
Right Hemithorax: Clear costophrenic angle; no pleural fluid (no hemothorax).

Right Anterior Thorax (Pneumothorax): Complete absence of lung sliding at the right 2nd and 3rd intercostal spaces mid-clavicular line. M-mode confirms a distinct "barcode sign" (stratosphere sign). A lung point (transition zone between sliding and non-sliding pleura) is identified laterally at the mid-axillary line, confirming a partial right pneumothorax.
Left Hemithorax: Normal; normal lung sliding without pleural fluid (no hemothorax or pneumothorax).
Intraperitoneal free fluid within Morison’s pouch, the left subphrenic space, and the pelvis (highly suspicious for hemoperitoneum).
Right-sided anterior pneumothorax with a confirmed lateral lung point.

Blunt thoracic and abdominal trauma following a high-speed motor vehicle collision. Patient is hemodynamically stable. Evaluation for hemoperitoneum, hemothorax, pneumothorax, and pericardial effusion.

Real-time point-of-care ultrasound evaluation using phased-array and high-frequency linear transducers across the standard 8 EFAST zones: Right Upper Quadrant (RUQ), Left Upper Quadrant (LUQ), Suprapubic (Pelvic), Pericardial (Subxiphoid/Parasternal), and Bilateral Anterior Thoracic spaces.
RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT (RUQ) (Morison’s Pouch): No free fluid in the hepatorenal space, inferior liver tip, or right subphrenic space.
LEFT UPPER QUADRANT (LUQ) (Splenorenal): No free fluid in the splenorenal space, subphrenic space, or around the inferior spleen tip.
SUPRAPUBIC (PELVIS): Well-distended/catheterized urinary bladder. No anechoic free fluid in the rectovesical pouch (male) / pouch of Douglas (female).
Smooth pericardial interface without evidence of pericardial fluid, effusion, or cardiac tamponade physiology.

Right Hemithorax: Clear costophrenic angle; spine sign is absent above the diaphragm, with no supradiaphragmatic pleural fluid collection (hemothorax). Normal lung sliding visualized in real-time at the 2nd–4th intercostal spaces in the mid-clavicular line. M-mode confirms the classic "seashore sign"; no "barcode/stratosphere sign" or lung point identified.

Left Hemithorax: Clear costophrenic angle; spine sign is absent above the diaphragm, with no supradiaphragmatic pleural fluid collection (hemothorax). Normal lung sliding visualized in real-time at the 2nd–4th intercostal spaces in the mid-clavicular line. M-mode confirms the classic "seashore sign"; no "barcode/stratosphere sign" or lung point identified.
No sonographic evidence of intraperitoneal free fluid, pericardial effusion, hemothorax, or anterior pneumothorax.

Note: A negative EFAST does not exclude solid organ injury, retroperitoneal injury, or low-volume hemorrhage. Serial clinical evaluation or contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen/pelvis is recommended if clinically indicated.
Blunt trauma, morbidly obese patient with extensive subcutaneous emphysema following motor vehicle crash.
RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT (RUQ): Heavily degraded images due to diffuse subcutaneous air artifact and overlying bowel gas. The hepatorenal interface is only partially evaluated.
LEFT UPPER QUADRANT (LUQ): Heavily degraded images due to diffuse subcutaneous air artifact and overlying bowel gas. The splenorenal interface is only partially evaluated.
SUPRAPUBIC (PELVIS): Suboptimal visualization secondary to an empty urinary bladder and dense acoustic shadowing.
Subxiphoid window non-diagnostic due to abdominal distension/air; parasternal long-axis window utilized, showing no gross pericardial effusion.
Right Hemithorax: Diaphragmatic border is partially visualized without gross pleural effusion (no gross hemothorax). Normal lung sliding identified at the upper chest anteriorly (no pneumothorax).
Left Hemithorax: Diaphragmatic border is partially visualized without gross pleural effusion (no gross hemothorax). Normal lung sliding identified at the upper chest anteriorly (no pneumothorax).
Technically limited and indeterminate EFAST examination secondary to patient body habitus, severe bowel gas, and subcutaneous air.
Intraperitoneal free fluid cannot be confidently ruled out by POCUS alone.
Urgent contrast-enhanced CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis is recommended as soon as the patient’s hemodynamic status permits.

bank_title: EFAST SCAN REPORTING PHRASES BANK (BY ANATOMICAL SECTION)

subs.title: Normal
items: Average in size displaying homogeneous echo pattern with smooth regular surface.
No focal lesions or intra-hepatic biliary radicle dilatation. Portal vein is patent and not dilated.

subs.title: Liver Laceration
items: Ill-defined heterogeneous hypoechoic / hyperechoic intraparenchymal laceration of the [right / left] hepatic lobe, measuring ___ cm.

subs.title: Subcapsular Hematoma
items: Crescentic subcapsular collection indenting the hepatic contour, with absent internal vascularity on Color Doppler.

subs.title: Gall Bladder
items: Average distention with no intraluminal stones or sludge; wall is not thickened; common bile duct (CBD) is not dilated.
Collapsed gall bladder with thickened wall and pericholecystic fluid, which may be seen after trauma; clinical correlation is advised.

subs.title: Normal
items: Average in size displaying homogeneous echo pattern with intact capsule.
No focal lesions or perisplenic fluid collection.

subs.title: Splenic Laceration
items: Ill-defined heterogeneous hypoechoic / hyperechoic parenchymal laceration of the spleen, measuring ___ cm, with perisplenic free fluid.

subs.title: Subcapsular Hematoma
items: Crescentic subcapsular hematoma indenting the splenic contour, with absent internal vascularity on Color Doppler.

subs.title: Normal
items: Both kidneys are of average size, normal shape, parenchymal thickness, and echogenicity.
No gross stones, hydronephrosis, or back-pressure changes seen.
No gross para-aortic or pancreatic masses seen.

subs.title: Renal Injury
items: Perirenal hypoechoic / heterogeneous collection around the [right / left] kidney, suggestive of perinephric hematoma, with disrupted renal contour.

subs.title: Normal (Negative FAST)
items: No free intraperitoneal fluid (ascites / hemoperitoneum) detected in the hepatorenal (Morison's), splenorenal, or pelvic pouches.

subs.title: Hemoperitoneum (Positive FAST)
items: Anechoic to complex echogenic free intraperitoneal fluid in [Morison's pouch / splenorenal recess / pouch of Douglas], containing fine low-level internal echoes, suggestive of hemoperitoneum.
Free fluid measuring ___ cm in maximal depth, extending to the [right paracolic gutter / subphrenic space].

subs.title: Normal
items: Unremarkable pelvic organs and urinary bladder, with no free pelvic fluid.

subs.title: Bladder Injury
items: Underdistended bladder with free pelvic fluid, suspicious for bladder injury; further evaluation with CT cystography is recommended.

subs.title: Normal
items: No pericardial effusion. Cardiac activity present with normal chamber size.

subs.title: Pericardial Effusion / Hemopericardium
items: Anechoic to echogenic pericardial effusion measuring ___ mm, suspicious for hemopericardium in the trauma setting.
Right atrial / right ventricular diastolic collapse, suggestive of cardiac tamponade physiology; urgent clinical correlation is required.

subs.title: Absent Cardiac Activity
items: No organized cardiac activity detected at the time of the scan.

subs.title: Normal
items: Lung sliding is present bilaterally, with no features of pneumothorax.
No pleural effusion or hemothorax bilaterally; the spine sign is not seen above the diaphragm.

subs.title: Pneumothorax
items: Absent lung sliding on the [right / left] side with a barcode (stratosphere) sign on M-mode and absent B-lines.
A lung point is identified at the [region], confirming pneumothorax.

subs.title: Hemothorax / Pleural Effusion
items: Anechoic / complex pleural collection above the diaphragm on the [right / left] side, with loss of the diaphragmatic cut-off of the spine, measuring ___ cm, in keeping with hemothorax.
Associated compressive atelectasis of the adjacent lung.

subs.title: Normal Study
items: No free or localized intraperitoneal fluid collection, nor gross traumatic solid organ injury, could be detected at the time of the scan.
No pericardial effusion, pneumothorax, or hemothorax.

subs.title: Positive Study
items: Positive FAST: free intraperitoneal fluid in [region], suggestive of hemoperitoneum; urgent surgical consultation is recommended.
Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis is recommended if the patient is hemodynamically stable.

subs.title: Limitations & Communication
items: A negative EFAST does not exclude solid organ, hollow viscus, or retroperitoneal injury; CT or serial examination is advised if clinical suspicion persists.
Study limited by [bowel gas / body habitus / subcutaneous emphysema / patient motion].
